title: Edge GPU cabinet siting & utility matrix — APAC pilot (2026-06)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, quantitative siting + utility fit matrix for small-edge colocation cabinets intended for the APAC pilot (Singapore, Osaka). This sheet is a working workbook to verify circuit availability, thermal headroom, floor loading, and expected rack-level utilization for 1U/2U GPU server mixes.

Scope:
- Target sites: SG01 (primary), KIX01 (secondary)
- Cabinet footprint: 42U full-depth standard cabinets, option for 24U half-depth in some floors
- Server types in scope: 4x H100-80GB (server A), 8x H100-80GB (server B), 4x A100-80GB (server C)
- Time horizon: Q3 2026 pilot + 12-month scale projection

Assumptions (working):
- H100 TDP (sustained peak) modeled at 700W/GPU; A100 at 450W/GPU. Host overhead (PSUs, fans, NICs, NVMe) = 1.0–1.5 kW per server depending on config.
- Power provisioning planning uses a 1.25 overhead multiplier for PDUs/UPS losses and peak headroom.
- Cooling planning converts kW to BTU/hr using 1 kW = 3412 BTU/hr.
- Weight per populated rack: 800–1200 kg depending on PDU and cooling attachments.

Quick reference hardware power profiles:
- Server A (4x H100): GPUs 4 * 700W = 2800W; host + PSU = 1200W => server rated 4.0 kW nominal; planning value = 4.5 kW
- Server B (8x H100): GPUs 8 * 700W = 5600W; host + PSU = 1500W => rated 7.1 kW; planning value = 8.0 kW
- Server C (4x A100): GPUs 4 * 450W = 1800W; host + PSU = 1000W => rated 2.8 kW; planning value = 3.2 kW

Rack-level layout options (42U):
- Option 1 (dense H100): 4 x Server B (8x H100) per rack => 4 * 8.0 kW = 32.0 kW (planning) => requires 3-phase 63A breakers / dual PDUs per rack, cold-aisle containment mandatory.
- Option 2 (mixed): 6 x Server A (4x H100) + 4 x Server C (4x A100) => (6*4.5) + (4*3.2) = 27.8 kW => comfortable on 3-phase 50A per PDU pair if site supports 3x 32A legs.
- Option 3 (conservative): 12 x Server C (4x A100) => 12 * 3.2 = 38.4 kW (high) — reserve only for sites with 60A/leg infrastructure.

Electrical fit checklist (per rack):
- Available incoming service: single-phase 208V vs 3-phase 400V (site): SG01 = 3-phase 400V native; KIX01 = 3-phase 415V with local CT metering.
- Breaker capacity required (min): 3-phase 63A recommended for racks >24kW; 3-phase 32A acceptable up to ~12–15kW.
- PDU config: dual redundant PDUs, each fed from separate breakers/UPS banks.
- UPS/battery: for pilot, N+1 local UPS sized to support a 5-minute graceful drain at full load => UPS_kW = rack_kW * (5/60).
- Metering requirement: per-rack CT recommended for billing and thermal correlation.

Thermal & cooling notes (per rack):
- 30 kW rack => 30 kW * 3412 = 102,360 BTU/hr. Guaranteed CRAC capacity must be at least 120% of sustained dissipation when colocated with neighboring racks; recommend 1.25 containment headroom for hot-aisle recirculation.
- Cold-aisle containment strongly recommended for SG01 (space constrained). Use blanking panels and baffle strips.
- Ambient inlet target: 18–25 C; max allowable inlet 30 C for short bursts only.
- Water-cooled or direct-to-chip (D2C) considered for racks >30 kW per rack; otherwise ensure row-level cooling with 30 kW chill capacity per 3–4 racks.

Flooring & structural: 
- Tile load rating: verify 1500 kg per tile for cabinets >1000 kg. Confirm subfloor void for cabling & chilled water riser.
- Cable routing: top-of-rack preferred for power drops; reserve 200 mm conduit for PDU tails.

Capacity matrix (pilot projections — single rack equivalents):
| Site | Rack ID | Opt | Estimated rack kW (planning) | Circuit req (A/leg) | Cooling BTU/hr | Expected monthly avg util (%) | Notes |
| SG01 | R-12 | Option 1 | 32.0 kW | 63A | 109,184 | 55–75 | Primary pilot; requires cold-aisle containment |
| SG01 | R-13 | Option 2 | 27.8 kW | 50A | 94,922 | 40–65 | Mixed workload, lower sustained avg |
| KIX01 | R-05 | Option 2 | 27.8 kW | 50A | 94,922 | 30–50 | Backup site; limited floor tile rating in row 2 |

Projected capacity planning (12-month):
- Q3 2026: 6 racks provisioned (3 SG01, 3 KIX01) => initial usable DGPU capacity ~ (mix-weighted) ~ 360 H100-equivalent GPUs.
- Q4 2026: +12 racks if metrics (latency, cost-per-token) meet thresholds. Plan triggers: sustained avg util >= 60% and P95 latency < 220ms.

Risk register (top items):
- Electrical underprovision: risk that site 3-phase legs not balanced; mitigation: per-rack CT + onsite electrician pre-deploy test, reorder PDUs to balance phases. Owner: Diego Alvarez.
- Thermal recirculation causing hotspots: mitigation: deploy thermal sensors at inlet/outlet, floor smoke test, and reserve row-level portable AC as stopgap. Owner: Priya Nair.
- Shipping/customs delays for H100 inventory: mitigation: staggered procurement and secondary vendor agreements. Owner: Samir Venkataraman.

Action items (next 30 days):
1) Confirm breaker panel mapping for SG01 row 3 and supply electrician sign-off (Diego) — due 2026-06-14.
2) Order dual PDUs + CTs for pilot racks (Priya) — due 2026-06-18.
3) Create thermal sensor wiring plan and cadence for 1-week pre-deploy soak test (Samir) — due 2026-06-12.
4) Update site acceptance test (SAT) checklist to include inlet delta-T > 12 C as failure condition (Maya) — due 2026-06-15.

Telemetry & metrics to capture in pilot:
- Per-rack power (kW) sampled at 1s if possible; aggregate to 1m/5m ticks.
- Inlet/outlet temps per 1U band.
- GPU utilization, host CPU utilization, and PCIe error rates.
- Token throughput and p95 latency correlated with power step-ups.

Notes / open questions:
- Confirm local site allowed use of portable A/C or D2C installation timelines (ops/legal).
- Verify whether local utility can support temporary 60A/leg provisioning for burst windows.

Appendix: quick calc examples
- Example: Rack with 4x Server B => 4 * 8.0 kW = 32 kW. With 1.25 planning overhead => 40 kW electrical budget. If site provides 3-phase 400V @ 63A per leg => per-leg power = 400V * 63A * sqrt(3) approx 43.5 kW => meets 40 kW with limited headroom.
- BTU conversion: 32 kW * 3412 = 109,184 BTU/hr.

Contact & approvals:
- Primary author: Maya Chen (eng-private-deployments)
- Technical reviewers: Diego A., Priya N., Samir V.
- Ops sign-off required from site facilities and legal for cross-border equipment movement.
